title: This meme is so them
old_caption: That meme is SO them. If it's really an opening and you're not ready to be friends, send it to the people who'll laugh the loudest.

title: You owe them an apology
old_caption: Sometimes the check says send it. A real apology asks for nothing back, not even a reply. Say sorry, then let it be theirs.

title: Mutual friend's wedding next week
old_caption: Shared friends, one wedding, and you need to know if they're going. Your answer is the same either way. Go for the couple, and bring a friend.

title: You still have their keys
old_caption: Returning their stuff doesn't need a speech. Keep the logistics text short and kind, and take the big feelings to a friend.

title: One night, three almost-texts
old_caption: Three almost-texts in one long night, and number three is the big one. Big feelings need a person, not a send. Watch what Pisces does instead.

title: The holiday party test
old_caption: A holiday party, your ex's best friend, and three almost-texts. The real test comes on the ride home. Send a "home safe" to the people who asked.

title: Sunday alone, three traps
old_caption: A quiet Sunday has traps: the old brunch reminder, the two-person shelf, their show. Alone doesn't mean empty. Wait for trap three.

title: The "can we try again" draft
old_caption: The "can we try again" text, three honest questions, and a verdict. You can miss someone and still choose to move on. Wait for it.

title: When your friend is texting their ex
old_caption: Your friend is about to text their ex. Don't grab the phone. Ask the three questions and let them choose. Save this for your group chat.

title: Reply fast or don't bother
old_caption:
Does your bio read like a warning label?
Say what you offer instead: replying fast is lovely, patience is lovelier.
